doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Live music at Disney, Meredith Willson, Dean Kincaid
summary: Disney's live Town Square concerts, guest conductors, and Meredith Willson at the opening. Dean Kincaid, met at the Contemporary Hotel show band, becomes his champion.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: No go ahead. I wonder, you were playing music that nowadays they’re just piping in. Is that a fair statement?
Well back in those days you were playing live music for all these things, and I would guess that nowadays much of that music is just prerecorded and played.

Yeah. We did live concerts — the thing that I really enjoyed, we did live concerts in Town Square, set up in the Square. And the nice thing about it is Jim Christenson, the first leader, who is still around, had a lot of stuff that he published for Disney, and so we © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

played a lot of that. We had a lot of guest conductors, guys that wrote some of these marches that I’d never even met them. And of course Meredith Wilson was there for the grand opening for Disney. You know, he was the — and he hung out in the band room. He loved everything. I mean what a great guy. And so that was — and here I am from Rock Island, Illinois. I hadn’t met anybody. And looking back I mean my move from Rock Island to Orlando was the best career move I could have ever made anywhere. I mean I met everybody in the world. And the guy that put me on the map was Dean Kincaid. Famous sax player. Of course you know that. And they had, when Disney opened they had, on the top of the Contemporary Hotel, they had a place called the show at the top or something like that. And they had a 12-piece band playing for dancing, but also backing shows and a fine place to eat. So you could go there, I mean people from town could go there and have dinner, a nice dinner and dance a little bit, see The Four Freshmen, Mel Torme, Trini Lopez, people like that, semi-names, but that’s not fair to say I guess. But God I loved the Freshmen, one of my favorite groups of all time. But occasionally they would need a third trombone, they only had two in the band. So I made it known that I’d be interested. So I got an occasional call to go up there and play. Well Dean Kincaid was the baritone sax player. And it’s funny because Disney had also hired him to write some Dixieland lead sheets for some of these musicians who weren’t that familiar with trad music. And Dean Kincaid said yeah, he said, “I’ve got to get back” — So one night we were having a drink and he said, “Yeah I’ve got to get back to my hotel,” he says, “they’ve got me doing a bunch of these Dixieland 101 things.”
